openings.claim: Separate lateral registration from seal compression: two removable, padded strip assemblies grip the rim and present locating faces to the hatch edges, with cord retaining released components.
openings.delta: Change the load carrier from hatch-to-seal friction to edge-to-strip-to-rim bearing. Drill or cut only supplied strips; use their bolted pairs as removable assemblies. Avoid tightening the hatch left corner to resist sliding.
openings.prediction: Compared with the nearest rival, stronger compression-only retention, locating faces should reduce sideways displacement without reproducing the opposite-corner lift. This is a hypothesis; neither adequate bearing capacity nor disturbance tolerance is established.
openings.probe: First check whether the actual rim and hatch edges allow padded removable engagement and complete clearance on removal. If feasible within ninety minutes, fabricate one configuration using four strips, supplied bolts, pads and cord. Within twenty observation minutes, run ten opening/closure/pull trials, placing the supplied 1 mm card at the marked right contact for final closure. Record marked-position error, movement under 20 N, corner lift, reopening time and seal tears each cycle. Clear every assembly from the full opening when open. Reject if any outcome fails, engagement slips, permanent deformation appears, or seal damage occurs; stop before damage when apparent.
assumptions: Rim access, edge geometry and strip reach permit locating faces and padded gripping; these indispensable conditions are unspecified.
Supplied pads, bolts and strips have sufficient grip and bearing capacity at loads that do not permanently deform the fixture.
The disturbed closure can remain within 1 mm and reopen within 30 seconds without requiring increased corner compression.

assessment: One opening. Edge bearing addresses the stipulated sliding and preload-induced lift, but missing interface geometry prevents a feasibility claim. Ten trials include the required disturbed trial and stay within the twelve-trial cap. The proposal is a fabrication-and-observation probe, not deployment; failure to obtain suitable engagement defeats it without relaxing constraints.
